A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PMSR and retain the same principal method and experiments. All 23 pages of v5 and 24 pages of v6, including appendices, tables, figures and equations, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V5 reports original retrieval and VQA accuracy results, component ablations, trajectory analyses, sensitivity experiments and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V6 retains those empirical results and adds runtime optimization experiments, query and retriever comparisons, reasoning-behavior analysis and HotpotQA evaluation.

M1.justification: Appendix T introduces a text-only adaptation using a textual KB alone while preserving progressive retrieval and both query scopes. The principal multimodal algorithm and prompts remain unchanged; the newly emphasized record-isolated updates were already explicit in v5 Section 3.4.

E1.justification: Appendix T adds a focused text-only, multi-hop QA evaluation on HotpotQA dev, extending coverage beyond VQA. All six original VQA benchmarks remain; the additional InfoSeek and E-VQA subset experiments retain existing task coverage.

E2.justification: V6 substantially broadens supplementary comparator coverage: Table A14 evaluates Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B, Table A15 compares against CoT, RAG, IRCoT, Search-R1-7B and s3, and Table A11 adds a single-step RAG latency comparison. Original VQA comparator sets remain unchanged, and WebWatcher already participated in v5's trajectory comparison.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce concurrent retrieval and H100 timing conditions, subset-based query/retriever comparisons, multi-label LLM judgments of reasoning behavior, and LLM-based HotpotQA evaluation. Existing benchmark splits and metrics remain unchanged. Section 5's newly specified 20-pair multimodal-only ablation budget is additional documentation, without establishing that the earlier experiment changed.

E4.justification: Appendices P–S substantially expand supplementary validation through latency decomposition and optimization tests, concatenation versus entity-extraction queries, reasoning-record behavior labeling, and replacement with an MLLM-based retriever. These examine previously untested design choices and mechanisms while retaining the earlier ablations, robustness analyses and qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables continue point-estimate reporting; behavior-label percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores remain unchanged after matching moved tables. Substantial new results include HotpotQA accuracy of 59.8, composition-label rates of 48.0%/50.5%, and query/retriever subset scores. Appendix P retains the 17.20-second vanilla timing and adds 11.61/4.33-second results under concurrent and concurrent-plus-H100 configurations. Table A9 also adds WebWatcher's previously unreported 12.1% stable-correct and 4.9% conflict shares.

T1.justification: The method equations, similarity definitions, saturation criterion and web-query formulation remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions and VQA performance claims. The introduction highlights record isolation and dual-scope querying more explicitly, but their scientific meaning was already present in v5. Broader text-only applicability is discussed in the new appendix rather than redefining the main claims.

C2.justification: New interpretations support concatenation over more complex query transformations, qualify the usefulness of an MLLM-based retriever, and extend applicability to text-only QA. Appendix P replaces proposed optimization benefits with measured discussion. Section 8 remains unrevised despite Appendix S now integrating an MLLM-based retriever.

D1.justification: Section 5 clarifies retrieval-budget allocation, including 20 image-text pairs for multimodal-only ablations. Appendix P documents concurrent retrieval, Qwen3-VL-8B decoding and H100 hardware, but removes the earlier Xeon CPU identification. Existing prompts, indexing and deduplication details are retained; several new subset sizes and judging details remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V6 adds references to s3, Search-R1, Qwen3-VL-Embedding and HotpotQA, extending discussion toward text-only search agents and MLLM-based retrieval. The main related-work positioning remains stable. Updating IRCoT from its preprint to its ACL publication does not introduce a different cited work.

P1.justification: Localized introduction and method rewrites emphasize record isolation and query roles. The two accuracy subsections exchange order, acknowledgments are added, and Appendix P is rewritten with subsections before new Appendices Q–T. Most existing prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V6 adds seven compact appendix tables, A9–A15, including a tabular presentation of the existing trajectory comparison. Main Tables 3 and 4 exchange numbering and placement, with accompanying page reflow. Existing diagrams, prompt figures and qualitative-case figures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V6 makes the efficiency and design rationale more assessable: Appendix P supports v5's proposed optimizations with measured timings, while Appendices Q–S directly test query design, reasoning behavior and retriever choice. These benefits are limited by unspecified subset sizes and judging details, plus Section 8's stale claim that MLLM-based retrievers are not integrated. The retained core evidence and useful supplementary tests support a modest net improvement.
